notes: Philadelphia Fair Workweek (Phila. Code ch. 9-4600) covers retail, food and hospitality employers with 250+ employees and 30+ locations worldwide, for employees working in Philadelphia.
Right to rest: no shift less than 9 hours after the previous day's shift unless the employee consents and is paid $40 (extra key premium_flat_dollars).
No city minimum-wage rule recorded for private employers (Pennsylvania state minimum wage applies).

Predictability pay (FAQ Predictability Pay Q4, § 9-4603): added time = 1 h at the employee's rate of pay; change of date, time, or location = 1 h each (the chart lists them separately; encoded per attribute, conservative); subtracted or cancelled hours (incl. on-call not called in) = >= 1/2 x rate for hours not worked. No pay for changes under 20 minutes at either end, or for changes made within 24 h after the posting deadline.

Call-out repair (FAQ Q12-14): asking one employee to cover or stay late requires written consent AND predictability pay; a Written Mass Communication sent to all employees qualified to fill the shift, used only for hours another employee cannot work, stating that accepting is voluntary and they may decline, is exempt. Shift trades consented by Written Communication are exempt.
'Written Communication' = print or electronic means incl. email, text messages, scheduling applications (FAQ Q5).
Coverage: retail, food or hospitality establishments with 250+ employees worldwide and 30+ locations worldwide (§ 9-4601), counting full-time, part-time and temporary employees.

exemption_message_must_state: the employee has the right to decline the hours
params.exemption_note: Exempt if the employee "volunteers to work additional hours in response to Mass Written Communication" used only for hours another employee cannot work, making clear "accepting such hours is voluntary and employee has the right to decline".

rules.summary: Philadelphia (250+ employees and 30+ locations worldwide): after the 14-day posting, 1 hour of pay for added time and for each change of date, time or location; half pay for hours cut or cancelled. Covering an absent coworker via a written mass communication is exempt.
